axes.brief:
An elected constitutional framework coexists with dominance by the Prosperity Party, restricted opposition, internal conflict and weak effective independent checks. Formal rights and parliamentary removal procedures are not evidence of fully competitive national accountability. Focused review prioritises implemented competitive renewal and effective oversight; formal powers in controlled institutions are not automatically democratic accountability.
Focused six-question reassessment: Parliamentary government and professional administration exist under dominant-party and conflict conditions. Formal emergency approval is qualified by weak practical checks; no independent signature-triggered binding national law mechanism is established.
